physicalNotes: No radius or mass of Earendel is recorded here: its package frames it at 248,585 pc (object.json worldFrame.bodyRadiusM), half the short side of its picture at its distance, a presentation value.

sources.position: Welch et al. (2022), A highly magnified star at redshift 6.2, Nature 603, 815 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.14866); text: a highly magnified star sitting atop the lensing critical curve at RA, Dec = 01:37:23.232, -8:27:52.20 (J2000), designated WHL0137-LS
sources.distance: Comoving distance of the redshift z = 5.926 (Pascale et al. (2025), Is Earendel a Star Cluster?: Metal Poor Globular Cluster Progenitors at z ~ 6, arXiv:2507.05483) in the Planck 2018 cosmology: 8393236234.589988 pc, from Astropy 8.0.1 Planck18.comoving_distance (Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A6, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209). The project's convention for objects placed by redshift (packages/bake/cli/prepare-catalogue-points.mts).
sources.properMotion: Zero: the object is held at its published position; no motion across the sky is applied.
sources.radialVelocity: c z for the redshift z = 5.926: the redshift written as a velocity, not a motion through space. Pascale et al. (2025), Is Earendel a Star Cluster?: Metal Poor Globular Cluster Progenitors at z ~ 6, arXiv:2507.05483 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.05483); abstract: a spectroscopic redshift of the Sunrise galaxy, z = 5.926 ± 0.013, from NIRSpec PRISM spectroscopy.
